title: The local ring of a fibre ring is the localization modulo p, by the natural map
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fibre ring and $j:B\to C$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Let $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$; let $B_{\mathfrak q}$, $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ be the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$ the ideal of $B_{\mathfrak q}$ generated by the elements $\varphi(a)/1$, $a\in\mathfrak p$. Then the map $\theta:B_{\mathfrak q}\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$, $b/s\mapsto j(b)/j(s)$ ($b\in B$, $s\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$), is a well-defined ring homomorphism, it is surjective, and its kernel is $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$; so it induces a ring isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{\mathfrak Q}$ sending the class of $b/s$ to $j(b)/j(s)$.

proof.text: Put $D=(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B$, with localization map $i:B\to D$, and $I=\mathfrak pD$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient], the canonical $B$-algebra isomorphism $e:C\to D/I$ sends $j(b)$ to the class of $i(b)$. Let $\overline{\mathfrak Q}=e(\mathfrak Q)$ and let $\mathfrak r$ be its inverse image under $D\to D/I$. Then $I\subseteq\mathfrak r$, and $i^{-1}(\mathfrak r)=j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$. The natural image of every $a\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ is a unit in $D$, so $\varphi(a)\notin\mathfrak q$; the image of every $a\in\mathfrak p$ is zero in $D/I$, so $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak q$. Thus $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$, and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ and the ideal $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$ in the statement are well defined.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](2) to $B\to D$ and the prime $\mathfrak r$. Its hypothesis holds since $D$ is the localization of $B$ at the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$. It gives the natural isomorphism $u:B_{\mathfrak q}\to D_{\mathfrak r}$ with $u(b/s)=i(b)/i(s)$. As $u(\varphi(a)/1)=i(\varphi(a))/1$, the ideal generated by these elements for $a\in\mathfrak p$ is carried exactly to $ID_{\mathfrak r}$ (both ideals have the displayed generators). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], the natural map $D_{\mathfrak r}\to(D/I)_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}$ is surjective with kernel $ID_{\mathfrak r}$ and sends $d/t$ to the class of $d$ over the class of $t$. The isomorphism $e:C\to D/I$ identifies $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ with $(D/I)_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}$ by applying $e$ to numerators and denominators; its inverse takes the image of $j(b)$ to $j(b)$. Therefore the composite $B_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{u}D_{\mathfrak r}\to(D/I)_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ sends $b/s$ to $j(b)/j(s)$, is surjective, and has kernel $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: The composite in Step 2 is the displayed formula for $\theta$; because it is a composite of ring homomorphisms, it is well defined and preserves sums, products and $1$. Its proved surjectivity and kernel give the induced ring isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ by the first isomorphism theorem, and the formula for the induced map is still $[b/s]\mapsto j(b)/j(s)$.

lean.statement: theorem Fiber.localRingHom_surjective_ker_quotientEquiv {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (Q : Ideal (p.Fiber B)) [Q.IsPrime] : let j : B →+* p.Fiber B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom let q : Ideal B := Q.comap j let θ := Localization.localRingHom q Q j rfl let I : Ideal (Localization.AtPrime q) := (p.map (algebraMap A B)).map (algebraMap B (Localization.AtPrime q)) (∀ (b : B) (s : q.primeCompl), θ (Localization.mk b s) = Localization.mk (j b) ⟨j s, s.property⟩) ∧ Function.Surjective θ ∧ RingHom.ker θ = I ∧ ∃ e : (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸ I) ≃+* Localization.AtPrime Q, ∀ x : Localization.AtPrime q, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x) = θ x
